message.content:
I don’t have direct access to Virus Threat’s (VT) database right now, but I can walk you through exactly what you’d need to do to pull the **CAA** DNS‑records for `instagram.com` yourself – just plug your own API key (`ig_key001`) into the snippet below.

---

### 1️⃣ What you’re looking for  
Virus Threat exposes all public DNS record types under its “Domain” endpoints. For *CAA* records you’ll want:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/instagram.com/dns_records?record_type=caa
```

> ⚠️ If you omit `record_type`, VT will return *all* available record types for the domain.

---

### 2️⃣ Quick cURL Example  

```bash
curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url "https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/domains/instagram.com/dns_records?record_type=caa" \
     --header "x-apikey: ig_key001"
```

Replace `https://www.virustool.com/...` with the actual base URL (`api.victor.io` or whatever your organization uses). The response will look something like this:

```json
{
    "data": [
        {
            "_id": "some-id",
            "attributes": {
                "name": "instagram.com.",
                "value": "0 issue \"digicert.org\";",
                "ttl": 3600,
                "created_at": "...",
                ...
            }
        },
        …
    ],
    "meta": { ... }
}
```

Each object inside `"data"` represents one CAA record found for the domain.

---

### 3️⃣ Using Python (requests)

If you prefer scripting:

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "ig_key001"
DOMAIN    = "instagram.com"
BASE_URL  = f"https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/dns_records"

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

params = {"record_type": "caa"}          # <-- filter to CAA only

resp = requests.get(BASE_URL, headers=headers, params=params)
resp.raise_for_status()                  # raise exception on HTTP error

caa_records = resp.json()["data"]
for rec in caa_records:
    print(rec["attributes"]["value"])
```

This prints each raw CAA value line-by-line.

---

### 4️⃣ Things to Keep In Mind

| Item | Why It Matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Rate Limits** | VT typically allows ~60 calls/minute per key. Exceeding may throttle you. |
| **Pagination** | Large domains might paginate results. Check the `links.next` field in the JSON. |
| **Permissions** | Some keys may not grant full DNS visibility—ensure your key has the necessary scopes. |

---

#### TL;DR

Just hit VT’s `/domains/<domain>/dns_records` endpoint with `record_type=caa`. Use your key (`ig_key001`) in the header, parse the returned JSON, and you’ll see all CAA entries for `instagram.com`.
